pairs.why: Both put the pumpkin on weathered, peeling wood, which the clean real floors don't have, but A's chipped tabletop edge is the more texture-heavy of the two.
A sits on a plain plank floor like the rocking-chair and glove cards, while B adds a chipped, peeling table edge that reads too texture-heavy.
A's front edge is heavily chipped and weathered; B's floor is a bit cleaner and closer to the smooth wood on the real cards, though both pumpkins are nearly the same.
A's simple plank floor matches the real cards; B's table front is heavily chipped and peeling, which adds the extra texture the lessons mark down.
The two are very close, but A's bristles are slightly chunkier and more stylized, which matches the smooth, simple shapes of the real props.
A's straw is drawn in broad, smooth clumps, while B's head breaks into finer, hairier strands that read as too texture-heavy.
A keeps the bristles in chunky, smooth bundles; B's straw is finer and fuzzier, closer to a realistic texture than the real cards' clean finish.
B's bristles are chunky, smooth strands like the real cards' simple forms; A's broom head is finer and hairier, which reads as too texture-heavy.
